data.name: Oore CI
data.short: Mobile releases, on your own terms.
data.description: Build, sign, and distribute Flutter apps on your own macOS infrastructure. I started Oore to make my own release workflow less fragmented.
data.problem: Mobile release pipelines often become fragmented: build logic in one place, signing in another, and distribution as a separate workflow.
data.solution: Oore CI centralizes build orchestration, signing workflows, and internal artifact delivery into one self-hosted system designed for Flutter mobile teams.
data.highlights:
Build, sign, and publish Flutter apps to the App Store and Google Play from one pipeline
Shared signing library with per-workflow signing and publishing
Pipelines and workflows defined in .oore.yaml files in your repository
Daemon, CLI, and web UI, with concurrent builds per macOS runner

data.name: Chek
data.description: A reader for books and comics on iPhone, iPad, and the web, with an optional self-hosted server. Chek 2.0 is out on the App Store.
data.problem: Reading apps tend to tie your library to one store or one device, and self-hosted library servers rarely come with a reader that feels native.
data.solution: Chek reads your own files offline, with no account. It can also connect to a Chek server, or to Komga and Kavita through it, so your place follows you between devices.
data.highlights:
Native iPhone and iPad app, plus a web app at app.chek.page
Reads EPUB, PDF, CBZ, MOBI, AZW3, Markdown, and more, offline
Self-hosted Rust server with Docker images, OPDS 2, and WebAssembly source extensions
Chek Reader, the reading engine, published as a standalone Swift package
No ads, tracking, or analytics

data.name: Tagflow
data.description: A native rich content runtime for Flutter. Structured documents, HTML support, and live patches, without putting a web view between your content and your app.
data.problem: Dynamic content in Flutter often means choosing between a web view and custom rendering code. Structured content should not have to round-trip through HTML.
data.solution: Tagflow uses a shared document runtime for native content and HTML. Apps can validate trusted JSON, render native widgets, and apply patches as content changes.
data.highlights:
Native document rendering with an HTML adapter
Markdown, streaming content, and code blocks in 1.0.0-beta.1
Trusted JSON input with validation and content policies
Document patches for live content updates
Tables through the tagflow_table extension

data.name: gpuicn
data.description: Open-code components for Rust and GPUI. Add the source to your app, then shape the details to fit your interface.
data.problem: Native app interfaces need familiar controls, but a fixed component API can make small design changes hard to own.
data.solution: gpuicn brings the shadcn/ui approach to GPUI: editable component source, built on BaseGPUI, with idiomatic Rust APIs and themes.
data.highlights:
45 components with editable source, or use them as a crate and eject to edit
gpuicn CLI on crates.io: new, add, diff, eject, and shadcn theme import
Real GPUI previews in the browser through WASM and WebGPU
Lucide icons through gpui-icons, now on crates.io

data.name: Anpec
data.short: Know the device. Adapt the app.
data.description: Android device performance classification for Flutter apps, so features can adapt to the hardware they run on.
data.problem: A single experience for all Android devices can break UX quality on lower-tier hardware and waste resources on higher-tier devices.
data.solution: anpec classifies device performance at runtime so apps can apply feature flags and behavior tuning based on actual capability.
data.highlights:
Runtime performance classification for Android in Flutter apps
Supports capability-aware feature flags and fallback paths
Helps optimize animations, effects, and expensive processing
Simple integration as a focused plugin

data.name: Seisei
data.short: A little more certainty for AI.
data.description: Typed AI contracts for Dart and Flutter applications.
data.problem: Applications need clear expectations at the boundary between AI output and application code.
data.solution: Seisei explores typed contracts for that boundary in Dart and Flutter.
data.highlights:
Typed AI contracts
Dart and Flutter
Open source
